verdict.summary: OpenWeatherMap does not use OAuth, so there is no third-party app to register, no scopes, and no redirect URI. Access is one personal API key from a login-gated account page, and I found no review step for using it in an app. The open question is whether Composio accepts a plain API-key credential for this service.
verdict.time_to_first_connection: Minutes after sign-up, but a new key can take up to 2 hours to activate

gates.name: Personal API key (account-level)
gates.unlocks: Your own account can call OpenWeatherMap APIs with your personal key (appid parameter, or X-Api-Key header on some endpoints). This is the only authorization method described.
limits: Call limits apply to the whole account, not per key, so extra keys do not raise limits.
Free-tier figures from third-party sites: 60 calls/minute and 1,000,000 calls/month with no card. Verify on the pricing page.
One Call 3.0 reportedly requires a subscription with a valid card on file, even if a daily cap is set.
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes to sign up and verify email. A new key can take up to 2 hours to activate.

gates.name: No separate invited/test tier found
gates.unlocks: No test-user allowlist, development store, or unlisted-install mechanism was found. Other users can use the service only through their own keys or a key you share, which is a credential-handling decision, not a provider approval step.
limits: No install limits or user caps were found, and no 2025-2026 policy page covering them was located.
gates.time_to_reach: Not applicable as a distinct provider gate

gates.name: Public use of a key in an app (attribution licence)
gates.unlocks: Showing OpenWeather data to end users in an app, website, dashboard, or report. The main requirement is attribution to OpenWeather. No app-review queue was found for this.
limits: Attribution to OpenWeather is required when weather is shown to end users.
No marketplace app-review process for third-party apps was found. Confirm with OpenWeather before a commercial launch.
gates.time_to_reach: Immediate once attribution is in place. No review timeline found.

steps.title: Confirm there is no OAuth app to register
steps.detail: Do not look for a Client ID, Client Secret, or redirect URI for OpenWeatherMap. The provider documents API-key authentication only, and its OpenID discovery document is missing. Plan the integration around one API key.
gotchas: Composio has no OpenWeatherMap toolkit, so there is no managed OAuth app either.

steps.title: Create an OpenWeatherMap account
steps.detail: Go to the API keys page and sign up or sign in. Verify your email address when prompted.
gotchas: The API keys page requires sign-in; anonymous visitors are redirected to a sign-in page.

steps.title: Copy your personal API key
steps.detail: On the account's API keys page, copy the key listed under your account. Store it in a secrets manager, not in source code.
gotchas: A new key can take up to 2 hours to activate. Calls made before then will fail, which can look like a bad key.

steps.title: Test the key with one direct API call
steps.detail: Call a current-weather endpoint with your key in the appid query parameter, for example https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather?q=London&appid=YOUR_KEY. A JSON response confirms the key works. If you need a header instead, some endpoints also accept X-Api-Key.
gotchas: The header form is documented only by a third party for some endpoints, such as One Call 3.0. Use appid unless you have confirmed otherwise.

steps.title: Decide whether you need One Call 3.0
steps.detail: If you only need the basic weather endpoints, the free tier may be enough. If you plan to use One Call 3.0, add a card in the account billing area before you rely on it. Reported free-tier limits come from third-party sites, so check the provider's pricing page first.
gotchas: One Call 3.0 reportedly requires a card on file even with a daily cap set.

steps.title: Check whether Composio accepts an API-key credential here
steps.detail: In the Composio dashboard, look for a generic API-key or custom-credential option for OpenWeatherMap. Enter the key there if it is offered. If Composio does not support this, call the API directly from your agent code. This has not been verified against Composio's documentation.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: No redirect URI is needed for an API-key credential. The Composio callback URL applies only to OAuth flows, which OpenWeatherMap does not use.
Composio's toolkit catalog has no OpenWeatherMap entry, so do not expect a one-click connect button.

steps.title: Run the agent end to end with your key
steps.detail: Have the agent make a few representative calls, such as current weather, forecast, and any One Call endpoint you plan to use, using the stored key. Confirm the responses and note the rate of calls against the account-level limit.
gotchas: Limits are shared across all keys on the account, so a loop that retries on errors can exhaust the quota fast.

steps.title: Draft the attribution text for any user-facing use
steps.detail: If weather data will be shown to end users, draft an attribution line that credits OpenWeather and place it where users see the weather output. Review the wording against the developer guide before publishing.
gotchas: The developer guide's wording was taken from search snippets and probe excerpts. Re-check the exact text on the guide page.

steps.title: Confirm the licence for your use case with OpenWeather
steps.detail: Read the developer guide and terms for public or commercial display of weather data. If the product is commercial, or you are unsure the attribution licence covers it, contact OpenWeather before launch. No review queue was found, so there is nothing to submit.
gotchas: No marketplace app-review or timeline was found for OpenWeatherMap. Do not assume one exists or does not exist without checking.

steps.title: Ship with the key stored as a secret
steps.detail: Store the production key in your secrets manager or Composio credential store. Set up monitoring for 401 and 429 responses. Create a separate key only if you need one for auditing, since limits are account-wide.
gotchas: Extra keys do not raise call limits.

requirements.item: Registered OpenWeatherMap account with email verified
requirements.detail: Needed to see the API keys page and receive a personal API key.

requirements.item: Personal API key sent with every call
requirements.detail: Sent as the appid parameter. X-Api-Key works on some endpoints only.

requirements.item: Card on file for One Call 3.0
requirements.detail: Reported by community sources. Needed only if you use One Call 3.0.

requirements.item: Attribution to OpenWeather when showing weather to end users
requirements.detail: The main licensing requirement for displaying weather output in an app, website, dashboard, or report.

scopes.effect: The provider describes no scopes or permission tiers. One account-wide API key unlocks all subscribed products, so there is no per-scope review or consent screen.

blockers.symptom: No OpenWeatherMap toolkit in Composio, so no managed OAuth connect button.
blockers.cause: OpenWeatherMap is not an OAuth provider and Composio's catalog has no entry for it.
blockers.fix: Configure the key as an API-key credential if Composio offers one, or call the API directly from your agent.

blockers.symptom: One Call 3.0 calls fail or the subscription cannot be activated without a card.
blockers.cause: Community reports say One Call 3.0 needs a subscription with a valid card on file, even with a daily cap.
blockers.fix: Add a card in the account billing area, or use only the free endpoints.

blockers.symptom: A new key returns errors right after creation.
blockers.cause: Keys take up to 2 hours to activate automatically after registration.
blockers.fix: Wait up to 2 hours and retry before assuming the key is wrong.

composio.note: Composio has no OpenWeatherMap toolkit, so there is no managed OAuth app and no scopes. Do not plan an OAuth app registration. Use an API-key credential if Composio supports one for this service; that support has not been verified. Otherwise call the API directly.

evidence.claim: Composio's toolkit catalog has no entry for OpenWeatherMap, so no managed OAuth is offered through Composio.
flags: no probe was run against this host

evidence.claim: The OpenWeatherMap main API page is live and publicly reachable, and it points visitors to an API key sign-up and documentation rather than an app-registration flow.
evidence.quote: Get API Key Explore API Docs

evidence.claim: The OpenID Connect discovery document at the OpenWeatherMap domain is missing (the probe returned not found), consistent with no OAuth or OIDC identity layer.
The OpenWeatherMap marketplace page is a historical weather data product store, not a developer app directory; no app review or listing process for third-party OAuth apps was found there.
evidence.quote: Historical Weather Data Archives | Weather Marketplace

evidence.claim: A third party reports free-tier limits of 60 calls per minute and 1,000,000 calls per month with no card, while One Call 3.0 gives 1,000 calls per day but requires a card on file.
evidence.quote: allow 60 calls/minute and up to 1,000,000 calls/month with no credit card

evidence.claim: A community forum post says the One Call 3.0 subscription requires a card on file, even when a daily cap is set to stay within the free allowance.
evidence.quote: requires an OpenWeather subscription with a valid credit card on file

evidence.claim: OpenWeather's developer guide says that displaying weather to end users in an app is a 'Produced Work' whose main licensing requirement is attribution to OpenWeather.
The official guide describes an attribution-based licence for displaying weather output, with no app-review step, and nothing in the material found refers to a review queue.
evidence.quote: If you use OpenWeather data to show weather information to end users, for example in an app, website, dashboard, or report

evidence.claim: OpenWeatherMap's official FAQ says every API call must carry the user's personal API key as an appid parameter, which is the only authorization described.
evidence.quote: we require you to use your unique API key in each API call

evidence.claim: The official FAQ says an account is issued a personal API key after registration and email verification, and that keys can be found on the account's API keys page.
evidence.quote: you will receive your personal API key (APPID)

evidence.claim: The official FAQ says a new API key activates automatically up to two hours after registration.
evidence.quote: activated automatically, up to 2 hours after

evidence.claim: The official FAQ says API call limits apply at the account level across all keys, so creating extra keys does not raise limits.
evidence.quote: API call limits are applied at the account level, not per API key.

evidence.claim: The official FAQ describes no scopes or permission tiers: one account-wide key unlocks all subscribed products, so there is no per-scope review.
evidence.quote: Any API key associated with your account can be used with all subscribed products.

evidence.claim: The official weather maps documentation says its endpoint requires only API key authentication.
evidence.quote: It requires only the API key authentication.

evidence.claim: A third-party integrator (dltHub) documents that some endpoints, such as One Call 3.0, also accept the key in an X-Api-Key header.
evidence.quote: some specific endpoints (such as One Call 3.0) also support passing it via an 'X-Api-Key' request header

evidence.claim: The API keys page redirects anonymous visitors to a sign-in page, so key issuance sits in a login-gated account area rather than a public app-creation portal.
evidence.quote: You need to sign in or sign up before continuing.

open_questions: Web fetching was limited in this research run, so the wording of the FAQ, appid, guide, weathermaps and pricing pages rests on search snippets and probe excerpts. Re-check the exact text before relying on it.
Whether Composio supports a generic API-key credential for OpenWeatherMap was not verified against Composio's documentation.
No developer-portal page for registering a third-party app was found. The only developer surface located is the login-gated account dashboard.
No 2025-2026 changelog or policy page about install limits, distribution rules, or unlisted-app caps was found. Whether any cap exists is unanswered.
No marketplace app-review requirements or timelines were found for OpenWeatherMap. Review-process results from other providers were not used.
Current free-tier limits and One Call 3.0 card requirements come mainly from third-party sites. Verify on the provider's pricing page.
